4 ارقصهُ [He made him to dance; or to play, or sport;] trans. of 1. (Msb.) You say, أَرْقَصَتْ وَلَدَهَا, (S, A,) or صَبِيَّهَا, (M,) She (a woman, S, M) [danced, or dandled, her child; or] made her child to leap or spring or bound [in her arms or on her knee]; (S, M;) as also ↓ رقّصتهُ , (S, M, A,) inf. n. تَرْقِيصٌ: (S, A:) or the latter verb has an intensive signification. (Msb.) ―
-b2- ارقص بَعِيرَهُ (tropical:) He made his camel to go in the [ambling] manner termed خَبَبٌ: (S, M, A, K:) and the same, (TA,) or ↓ رقّصهُ , (M,) he made him (i. e. his camel) to leap, spring, or bound. (M, TA.) ＝
-A2- See also 5.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
